title: Remove Non Friable Asbestos
description: This Course of competency specifies the outcomes required to remove non-friable asbestos containing material (ACM).
It includes preparing, containing and removing non-friable ACM, and knowledge of decontamination and disposal requirements.

When asbestos containing materials (ACM) are present, or even suspected of being present in the workplace, only qualified personnel are permitted to safely manage or remove it. Any worker removing more than 10m² of non-friable (also known as ‘bonded’) asbestos must be appropriately trained, as outlined in the Work Health & Safety Regulation 2011 and the Code of Practice for the Safe Removal of Asbestos. Non-friable asbestos materials include asbestos cement sheeting, often called fibro, used in many buildings before 1990. The sheeting was used for cladding, roofs and fences and can often be found as backing boards in wet areas like kitchens and bathrooms.

title: Certificate III in Telecommunications Technology
description: The ICT30519 Certificate III in Telecommunications Technology is a nationally recognized qualification in Australia for telecommunications technology operators.

title: Follow Work Health and Safety and Environmental Policy and Procedures.
description: This unit describes the performance outcomes, skills, and knowledge required to use organizational risk control procedures when working with a risk of exposure to radio frequency electromagnetic radiation (RF-EMR).  It applies to those working in environments where there is a risk of exposure to RF-EMR, such as telecommunications and broadcasting sites.

title: Install, maintain and modify customer premises communications cabling
description: This unit describes the skills and knowledge required to safely install, maintain, and modify communications cabling on customer premises according to the Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) ‘restricted’ Cabling Provider Rules.  It applies to cabling terminated on sockets and network termination devices (NTDs) of indoor and external metallic cable in aerial or underground situations.  The work includes connecting telecommunications devices such as telephony systems, security alarm panels, and fire control panels.  Typical customers include domestic, small offices, home offices, and small businesses.  Licensing, legislative, regulatory, and certification requirements apply, and all customer cabling work must be performed by a registered cabler.

title: Install, maintain and modify customer premises communications cabling: ACMA Open Rule.
description: This unit covers the skills and knowledge needed to safely install, maintain, and modify customer premises communications cabling following the Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) ‘open’ Cabling Provider Rules.  It applies to small, medium, and large commercial or industrial installations involving telephone sockets, multi-pair cables, backbone cabling, and advanced termination modules.  The unit includes managing aerial, underground, and internal cabling work on private and public property for existing networks or upgrading networks (e.g., convergence to next-generation networks).  Licensing and regulatory compliance is mandatory, with work conducted by ACMA-registered cablers.  The unit requires pre-requisites: ICTTEN208 (Use electrical skills when working with telecommunications networks) and ICTWHS204 (Follow work health and safety and environmental policy and procedures).

title: Use electrical skills when working with telecommunications networks
description: This unit describes the skills and knowledge required to use electrical skills in working with analog and digital cabling and wireless networks in telecommunications.  It applies to entry-level workers performing basic testing, circuit building, and evaluation of cable and wireless devices.  Work may occur in domestic, commercial, or industrial environments.

title: Follow Work Health and Safety and Environmental Policy and Procedures.
description: This unit covers the skills and knowledge required to follow workplace health, safety, and environmental procedures in an ICT environment.  It includes identifying hazards, assessing risks, and implementing control measures to ensure a safe working environment.  It prepares individuals to comply with legislative requirements and organizational policies relevant to health, safety, and environmental practices.

title: Install, terminate and certify structured cabling installation.
description: This unit involves the skills and knowledge required to place, secure, and terminate structured cabling for both indoor and outdoor installations.  It covers structured cabling installations for telecommunications including digital and analog telephony, data, video, digital broadcasting, computer networks (LANs, WANs), and multimedia systems.  This unit also includes certifying the installation to meet industry standards and client requirements.  Installations are carried out in domestic, commercial, or industrial premises as part of telecommunications network connections.

title: Install and terminate coaxial cable.
description: This unit covers the skills and knowledge required to install and terminate coaxial cable on client premises in various communications applications.  Applications include digital and analog telephony, data networks, video, digital broadcasting, cable television (CATV), closed-circuit television (CCTV), and other telecommunications systems.  It involves the correct handling, installation techniques, termination to standards, and testing of coaxial cables to ensure quality and compliance.

title: Install, test and terminate optical fibre cable on customer premises.
description: ICTCBL322 covers the skills and knowledge required to install, test, and terminate optical fibre cable used for telecommunications on customer premises.  This includes different types of terminations such as direct termination, fusion splicing, and mechanical splicing.  The unit applies to new installations, upgrades, and maintenance work in domestic, commercial, and industrial settings.  Communications applications include digital and analog telephony, data, video, digital broadcasting, computer networks, LANs, WANs, and multimedia systems.  Compliance with licensing, legislative, regulatory, and certification requirements is essential.  Work must be performed by registered cablers under Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) rules.

title: Use optical measuring instruments.
description: This unit describes the skills and knowledge required to set up and use hand-held optical communications instruments to perform installations, upgrades, and fault-finding on optical equipment.  It is designed for telecommunications lines workers who use hand-held optical measuring instruments.  The tasks include preparing for optical measurements, conducting tests, recording results, and interpreting data to ensure optical systems perform optimally.

title: Work safely on live optical fibre installations.
description: This unit describes the skills and knowledge required to work safely on a live optical fibre installation to test and commission a wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) system.  It involves understanding the dangers of live optical fibre cables and ensuring safety protocols are followed when working on such systems.  The unit applies to technicians working on telecommunications systems involving live optical fibre networks.  It covers testing, commissioning, and fault finding on live optical fibre components with an emphasis on safety.

title: Inspect, clean and handle optical fibre cable and connectors
description: The unit ICTTEN318 titled "Inspect, clean and handle optical fibre cable and connectors" describes the skills and knowledge required to inspect and clean optical fibre connectors and follow correct handling and placement practices for optical fibre cables.

title: Install, test and terminate optical fibre cable on customer premises
description: This unit describes the skills and knowledge required to install, test, and terminate optical fibre cable on customer premises for various communications applications.  It applies to installations in domestic, commercial, or industrial premises for digital and analog telephony, data, video, digital broadcasting, and other telecommunications systems.  The unit covers preparation, installation of cables, termination of optical fibres using fusion or mechanical splicing, testing cable joints for continuity and transmission loss, and completion of documentation.

title: Jumper metallic conductor cable in the access network
Install underground cable for communications applications
description: This unit covers the skills and knowledge required to install underground cable for various telecommunications applications within access networks or customer premises.  Installation includes placing cables in trenches, conduits, ducts, or pits, using appropriate techniques and equipment.  The job applies to telecommunications technicians working on underground infrastructure for data, voice, video, digital broadcasting, and other communication systems.  It involves following safety policies, industry standards, regulations, and manufacturer specifications.

title: Install underground enclosures and conduit.
description: This unit covers the skills and knowledge required to install underground enclosures and conduit systems.  Installation can be either direct buried or located in pits.  It is applicable for new or upgrade projects in telecommunications infrastructure.  Work involves handling and installing enclosures and conduits to protect underground cables and equipment.  It includes compliance with workplace health and safety, relevant codes, and regulations.

title: Haul underground cable for installation and maintenance work.
description: This unit involves the skills and knowledge required to haul underground cable for maintenance, new installations, or upgrades in access networks or customer premises.  It applies to technicians working with telecommunications underground cable systems.  Includes preparation, hauling cable in ducts, conduits, and trenches, handling cable safely, and complying with workplace health and safety requirements.

title: Construct underground telecommunications infrastructure.
description: This unit describes the skills and knowledge required to construct underground telecommunications infrastructure.  The infrastructure includes conduits, enclosures, pits, and trenches to support telecommunications cabling and equipment.  It involves preparing the site, installing conduits and enclosures, connecting sections, and ensuring compliance with safety standards and regulations.  Suitable for technicians working on new installations or upgrades of underground telecommunication networks.

title: Prepare to Work Safely in the Construction Industry
description: This unit of competency specifies the mandatory work health and safety training required prior to undertaking construction work. The unit requires the person to demonstrate personal awareness and knowledge of health and safety legislative requirements in order to work safely and prevent injury or harm to self and others. It covers identifying and orally reporting common construction hazards, understanding basic risk control measures, and identifying procedures for responding to potential incidents and emergencies. It also covers correctly selecting and fitting common personal protective equipment (PPE) used for construction work.
